More options, when you’re ready +

Liquid and debt funds can lose value; they are not bank deposits. Bonds have issuer and interest-rate risks. PPF has long-term access restrictions. Gold can diversify a portfolio but its price can fall, and it provides no guaranteed income. Check the terms of each product rather than relying on its category.

More complexity, more homework +

Crypto — sharp price swings and product-specific risks.

Futures & options — leverage can amplify losses; unsuitable as a simple starting point.

Individual stocks — fewer companies means more concentrated risk.

MYTH / 01

“Gold always goes up.”

Its price can fall, too. No asset owes you a return.

MYTH / 02

“An FD has no risks.”

Inflation, early-exit terms and bank risk still matter. Eligible bank deposits have insurance limits.

Read DICGC’s explanation ↗
MYTH / 03

“A SIP guarantees growth.”

A SIP is a regular investing method. The underlying investment still carries risk.

SEBI’s mutual-fund guide ↗

Show the maths and buying power +

The safe, steady and growth portions use illustrative annual rates of 4%, 6% and 9%. Of the non-growth portion, 20% is safe and 80% steady. The chart compares savings at 4%, an FD at 6%, and your weighted mix. Contributions arrive at month-end, with your chosen increase every 12 months. Rates are nominal, compounded monthly, and exclude taxes and fees. These are assumptions, not product quotes. The band uses the mix rate minus/plus 3 percentage points; it is a sensitivity illustration, not a probability range or a forecast. Actual outcomes can fall outside it.

What drives this replay? +

Both paths start with your chosen allocation. Growth falls 30% in year 1. Later growth returns are +18%, +12%, +8% in the recovery example, or −10%, +2%, +3% in the prolonged downturn. Safe money earns 3% and steady money 5% each year. The cash path moves only growth holdings into cash immediately after year 1 and earns 3% thereafter. Neither strategy always wins.
